report_01: Each point is one biological replicate. A: available human transcript sites after requiring ≥20 reads in each contributing sequencing run. B: percentage predicted modified (score ≥0.5) among the same 26,024 sites observed in all 17 replicates.
report_02: Central-position signal features at predicted modified minus predicted unmodified sites, matched within each biological replicate by the full 7-mer and read coverage (ratio ≤2). Each dot is one replicate’s median paired difference; horizontal bars are medians across 17 replicates. Colours identify cell lines. The three motifs contain 5,316 matched pairs in total.
report_03: A: all 21 cell-line pairs. Mean absolute score differences between and within cell lines use identical sites with ≥2 biological replicates per cell line and at most twofold differences in read coverage. B: number of cell lines in which every replicate predicts a site as modified; 25,345 common sites with no such cell line are omitted. Other cell lines may have mixed predictions.
report_04: A: metagene profiles with 10 bins per region for 170 shared predicted m6A sites and 24,356 analysed sites on fully annotated coding transcripts. Each curve sums to 100%; the orange background matches the shared sites’ contribution from each gene. B: the six highest-ranked genes among 870 with ≥10 common sites on one representative transcript. Colour shows the mean replicate fraction for each cell line; parentheses give analysed-site counts.
report_05: A: one comparison per gene, ranked using only the initial biological replicate from each cell line (lowest replicate number). Remaining replicates assess the same sites. Orange points reverse direction; the dashed line is equality. B: RNASEK scores at the three selected transcript sites in every observed biological replicate. Positions are equally spaced for readability, with small horizontal offsets to separate replicates. The HEYA8 − H9 mean difference falls from +0.303 to +0.079. The SAMD4B and C20orf24 compact layout shows their selected-site scores and read coverage.
appendix_01: A: the 17-replicate Spearman matrix on the same 26,024 sites, ordered by average-linkage clustering of 1 − correlation. r denotes biological replicate number. The scale starts at 0.75. B: every eligible technical- and biological-replicate pair, using its shared sites. Bars are medians. Pairwise sites differ from the complete common-site set in A; pairs can share replicates.
appendix_02: All 18 DRACH motifs among the 26,024 common sites. Each entry is the fraction scoring ≥0.5, averaged equally over biological replicates in that cell line. The motif-specific number of common sites is shown beside each row and is identical across cell lines. T is retained from the reference sequence notation (U in RNA). Matched signal comparisons additionally match the two outer bases of the 7-mer.
appendix_03: Mean prediction-score differences for the three highest-ranked distinct genes selected using initial samples. Each row keeps the same cell-line contrast and three transcript sites in initial and additional samples. At each site, available biological replicates are averaged within each cell line; site differences then receive equal weight. Hollow orange and filled blue points denote initial and additional samples; connectors link the two estimates, and the dashed line is zero. One initial sample contributes per cell line. Counts on the right give additional samples per site in the listed cell-line order; ranges indicate unequal observation across sites. Individual-site scores and read coverage are shown in the gene-specific figures.
appendix_04: The second and third genes selected by the same initial-replicate ranking as RNASEK. A–B: scores at the fixed three sites per gene. C–D: mean eligible-run read counts at those sites (log scale). SAMD4B nearly loses its mean difference in additional replicates; C20orf24 retains direction at only one of three sites.
appendix_05: A: fate of the original 181 shared predictions after rebuilding replicate means at each read-coverage cutoff. New predictions (3 at 30 reads; 2 at 50) are excluded from these stacks. B: all six comparisons involving Hct116, before and after excluding replicate 3 run 1, which overlaps Dataset 0. Each pair uses identical retained coordinates before and after exclusion. In two comparisons, between-cell-line variation exceeds within-cell-line variation only after exclusion.
